question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Which of the following is a basis of the eigenspace corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3?$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are free variables. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the required basis is

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}.
$$
